title: Faith and Truth - Episode 6: Abiding in the Vine

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome again to our SleepFit podcast series. This is Faith and Truth - Episode 6: Abiding in the Vine. I'm Sarah Mitchell. <short pause> And tonight... is a bittersweet one. <short pause> This is the final episode of our series. <chuckle> But don't worry... <short pause> this isn't goodbye forever. <short pause> I'm sure we'll meet again.
It's been a quiet joy to spend these evenings with you. <short pause> So before we go, I'd like to ask one last question... <short pause> what if staying close matters more than trying harder?

Jesus spoke these words to his disciples on the last night before his crucifixion. <short pause> He knew they were about to face confusion... and fear. <short pause> And the image he gave them wasn't a battle plan. <short pause> It was a vine.
I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman. <long pause>

A vine isn't something you conquer, or master. <short pause> It's something you live in relationship with. <short pause> The branch doesn't produce fruit by straining, or willpower. <short pause> It produces fruit by staying connected... to the source of life.
And then Jesus makes the comparison direct.
I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing. <long pause>
Notice how that verse ends. <short pause> Without him... we can do nothing. <short pause> Not some things poorly. Not most things with difficulty. <short pause> Nothing.

That's a hard word, in a world that celebrates self-reliance. <short pause> But it's also a deeply freeing one. <short pause> Because if the branch can't produce fruit on its own... then the branch isn't to blame when it struggles. <short pause> The question is never, am I working hard enough? <short pause> The question is... am I connected?
There's one word Jesus repeats in this passage more than any other. <short pause> Abide.

It's an old word, and it simply means to remain. To stay. To dwell. <short pause> Not to visit now and then, or check in when things get desperate. <short pause> But to live in a place... to make it your home.
Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: This isn't a technique. It isn't a spiritual discipline to squeeze into an already crowded life. <short pause> It's about where you live. <short pause> It's about turning your whole self toward this one connection.

And Jesus says the Father is the gardener. <short pause> He prunes the branches, so they can bear more fruit. <short pause> Pruning can feel like loss. <short pause> But the gardener isn't punishing the branch. <short pause> He's caring for it... clearing away what hinders, so that life can flow more freely.
And tucked into this passage is a beautiful promise.
If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you. <long pause>

When you remain in him, and his words remain in you... your desires begin to line up with his. <short pause> You start to want what he wants. <short pause> And the asking and the receiving flow naturally... out of the relationship. <short pause> This isn't a formula for getting what you want. <short pause> It's what happens when you're so close to him... that his life becomes yours.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So what does this mean for you tonight? <short pause> Maybe you're lying here thinking about all the ways you fell short today. <short pause> The things you meant to do. The patience you didn't have. The words you wish you could take back.
The vine says... stop judging yourself as if you were supposed to produce fruit on your own. <short pause> You were never meant to.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Maybe you're exhausted from trying to be enough... do enough... fix enough. <short pause> The vine says... the branch doesn't try harder. <short pause> The branch stays close.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Maybe you're worried you're not spiritual enough. That your prayers are too scattered. That you don't read Scripture enough, or understand it well enough. <short pause> The vine says... this isn't about your performance. <short pause> It's about his life, flowing into you.

Abiding doesn't mean you never move. <short pause> It means you move from a place of connection... instead of a place of striving. <short pause> You don't have to manufacture love, or joy, or patience. <short pause> Those are fruits that grow... when you're drawing life from him.
And if you feel dry right now... if the connection feels far away... that doesn't mean you've failed. <short pause> It might mean the gardener is at work, clearing away what's been blocking the flow.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Your job is simply to remain. <short pause> To turn your attention back to him, again and again, in the middle of ordinary life. <short pause> To let his words settle into you. <short pause> To admit your need... instead of pretending you're self-sufficient.
The branch doesn't worry about whether it's good enough. <short pause> It just stays attached to the vine. <short pause> And the life... flows.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: <exhales> Now, as we come to the end of this series... let's look back, just for a moment. <short pause> We began by learning to rest our weight on God. <short pause> We saw that his word is a lamp for the next step. <short pause> That the truth sets us free. <short pause> That even a mustard seed of faith is enough. <short pause> And that his promise is an anchor for the soul.
And tonight... all of it comes together in one picture. <short pause> You were never asked to carry the whole thing alone. <short pause> You are a branch... and he is the vine.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Thank you for walking through this series with me. <short pause> Whenever you need a quiet place to land, you can come back to any of these evenings. <short pause> And wherever you go from here... may you stay close.

Let's pray together. <short pause> Father, thank you that you don't ask us to produce fruit by our own effort. <short pause> Teach us what it means to abide... to stay close... to let your life flow through us. <short pause> And carry us gently, tonight and every night.
Rest well, friend. <short pause> Goodnight.
